views.name: 01_frontal.png
views.prompt: Edit the supplied protagonist robot concept into the MASTER FRONT VIEW for a consistent eight-view 3D modeling reference set. Preserve the exact original robot identity, helmet shape and narrow cyan visor, armor panels, ivory/off-white and graphite materials, orange shoulder and knee markings, proportions and moderate weathering. REQUIRED CHANGE: remove the entire pistol/blaster module from its anatomical right forearm. Replace that gun assembly with a normal slim articulated robot forearm and a complete five-finger mechanical hand matching the design of its existing other hand, mirrored naturally. Both arms must now have hands, and neither arm may carry any weapon, barrel, launcher or oversized weapon housing. Leave only a modest ordinary wrist joint; do not add accessories. Pose the same robot in a symmetrical neutral A-pose: upright torso, head straight, arms 25 degrees away from the body, elbows and wrists straight, hands relaxed open with separated readable fingers, feet parallel slightly apart, no contrapposto. Render EXACTLY ONE complete robot in a STRICT ORTHOGRAPHIC FRONT VIEW: camera directly ahead at torso height, no yaw, no tilt, no perspective, both shoulders/knees level and both feet aligned. Full body and all fingertips visible with generous identical margins, centered, vertical portrait canvas. Flat solid very light gray background, no environment, no horizon line, no floor grid, no labels, no text, no vignette, no drop shadows. Neutral even diffuse studio lighting, sharp details, restrained cyan emission, no bloom or dramatic reflections. Clear game character 3D render, not a sketch. This is a front modeling reference of the existing design, not a redesign. Only one view in this image.

views.name: 06_posterior.png
views.prompt: Image 1 is the approved FRONT design reference; image 2 is the REAR edit target. Correct image 2 so it is an anatomically consistent TRUE BACK VIEW, not a front body with its head reversed. Preserve image 2's rear helmet, back/shoulder casing, spine, overall silhouette, exact A-pose, framing, off-white graphite orange cyan style, background and lighting. Change ONLY rear-facing pelvic and leg and foot surfaces as necessary: replace the pointed frontal crotch/codpiece visible in image 2 with two modest rounded rear hip/glute armor plates separated by the spine; show the backs of the knees as recessed graphite mechanical hinge/piston cavities, NOT the large orange kneecap skid plates from the FRONT; the orange knee skid plates stay on the FRONT of the robot and should not face the rear camera. Rear thighs and calves show protected pistons and simple segmented rear plates, while preserving the existing leg dimensions. The feet must be observed from BEHIND: broad short flat dark heel bumpers at the bottom of the legs, toes pointing AWAY from camera and mostly hidden, not the long frontal toe caps facing the viewer. The back of the hands/forearms must be appropriate to the rear viewing direction. Both hands complete, five fingers, absolutely no weapon. This is the same robot rotated 180 degrees from image 1, without turning individual parts independently. Single full-body direct orthographic REAR view only, no labels or text.

views.name: 07_superior.png
views.view: Superior: cámara sobre la cabeza; frente del robot hacia abajo de la imagen.
views.prompt: Produce a TRUE ORTHOGRAPHIC TOP-DOWN VIEW of the exact unarmed robot in images 1 and 2 (front and back references), for a 3D modeling turnaround. The camera is at the zenith DIRECTLY OVER THE ROBOT'S HEAD, looking vertically down, exactly 90 degree elevation. It is NOT a high-angle front view. IMPORTANT GEOMETRY: the upright body is SEVERELY FORESHORTENED: most torso and ALL SHINS/THIGHS are naturally HIDDEN UNDER THE HEAD AND SHOULDERS. You must NOT show a long front chest, front thighs, kneecaps or tall standing legs in this image. Show the curved TOP surface of the ivory helmet at the center, tops of the orange shoulder armor to the sides, tops of arms and mechanical hands spread to both sides as projected from the original A-pose, two compact upper-back vent housings at the rear. At most small toe tips may peek beyond the lower silhouette. The full robot projects to a compact WIDE HORIZONTAL CLUSTER, much wider than its front-to-back depth. Front of robot points DOWN on the image, back points UP. The robot has not crouched, bent or changed pose; ONLY the camera moved overhead. Preserve the references' design and materials: ivory panels, dark graphite joints, orange shoulders, cyan accents, mechanical five-finger hands, no weapons. Plain light gray background, even illumination, no text, arrows, labels, ground plane or shadow. Keep a portrait canvas but let the genuinely top-down object occupy a SHORT WIDE centered shape with ample empty space above and below. One robot and one overhead view only. A modeling reference render, not a diagram or a flying pose.

views.name: 08_inferior.png
views.view: Inferior: referencia desde las suelas; frente del robot hacia arriba de la imagen.
views.prompt: Correct ONLY BOTH HANDS in this exact supplied image. The previous correction put the thumbs on the WRONG SIDE. Move each thumb to the OUTER SIDE of its hand, away from the robot's body. Use unambiguous IMAGE coordinates: the hand on the LEFT of the picture must have its ONE thumb sticking out from the LEFT outer edge of the palm, pointing left; the hand on the RIGHT of the picture must have its ONE thumb sticking out from the RIGHT outer edge of the palm, pointing right. REMOVE the short inward-pointing thumb currently on the edge nearest the robot/feet on each hand, leaving a smooth ulnar palm edge there. Preserve exactly FOUR long articulated fingers in a row extending downwards from each palm. End result is exactly FIVE separate digits per hand: four long fingers plus ONE outer thumb, zero inner thumbs, no sixth digit or thumb stump. Keep the original open palm circular mechanisms and matching mechanical ivory/graphite materials. Make the two hands coherent mirror counterparts. Keep EVERYTHING outside the hand silhouettes unchanged: same robot, wrists and arms, feet and sole tread, torso, helmet, pose, viewpoint, scale, 1024x1536 composition, lighting, background and weathering. Do not rotate or mirror the whole image. Do not change any other body part or add text. This is a surgical correction to the thumb placement and digit count on both hands.
